decisions: The user chose a slice of issue #68 (C15) for this change: (1) joined, retry and nomatch carry `from` and are accepted only from the current time keeper, as layouts are; (2) the device that pushed runs its own no-match timer; (3) the page shows the three join messages. Source: #68 Acceptance and Edge cases.

Out of scope by the user's choice: the join strip UI and tap-to-along mapping, refusing overlapping joins (#68 open question 6), narrowing retry to the clashing devices (open question 7), Undo (#85). The existing orb and net.push stay the trigger.

The `from` check is not forgery protection: `from` is set by the sender on a channel anyone with the room code can use. #68 says so; real protection is #24 (signed room messages). The check stops honest mistakes and stale time keepers.

The no-match limit is a named constant derived from WINDOW + DEADLINE plus a network margin, because a decision can come up to about 4.5 s after the first tap in a busy room (measured 4450 ms on the real net.js, evidence/day-07/raw/26-blind-repro-on-real-web.txt). A 2 s timer fired before a valid join (Qodo finding 24cbc11a on PR #86).

The timer is cancelled only by a result naming this device (joined with a or b = this device, nomatch with dev = this device, retry whose devs include it), because results are broadcast to the whole room. 'Couldn't tell who to join. Try again' stays until the next tap and is never replaced by this device's own 'No match'. A joined naming this device always wins.
notes: Expected behaviour is #68's Acceptance list under 'When only one device taps' and Edge cases 'nomatch is shown only on the device it names', 'joined, retry and nomatch are accepted only from the time keeper' and 'Joined with... shows only on the two devices the join names' (side from edgeA if this device is a, edgeB if b). Constraints: broadcasts use self:false, so the time keeper gets its own results by local emit (web/net.js:111,113,118); layouts are already accepted only from the leader (web/net.js:128-133). Must not break: npm run test:browsers direct and relay, and the time keeper is the only device that pairs pushes.
recent_work: Fix round after the previous local review (still uncommitted). Fixes only, chosen by the user: (1) one no-match timer per push: results carry the push time(s) they answer (nomatch t, joined tA/tB, retry pushes[{dev,t}]) and a device clears only that push's timer; check.js validators validJoined/validRetry/validNoMatch replace validDevList/validDev; (2) on the page a joined naming this device wins over a later nomatch or retry until this device pushes again; (3) 'Couldn't tell who to join. Try again' is sticky until the next push; (4) tighter tests (lone push gets the time keeper's nomatch under 4 s; the time keeper ignores results forged with its own id).

Test only, added after the fix round: a four-device two-browser check (A-B, C-D, then B-D join; messages only on the two named devices; all four hold the time keeper's 3 joins with no overlap and are one group; a print A puts down is visible on C). The overlap-and-drop case is left for the #68 strip work.

Left unchanged by the user's decision: accepting results from a time keeper that just left (the layout carrying the join is discarded by the same rule, so showing Joined would be wrong; the lost join is #61); strip, tap-position and keyboard tests (no strip in this slice); clock skew before a device's first clock reply.
